html:
The economic reforms launched by Vietnam's Communist Party in December 1986 that moved the country from central planning toward a market economy. The name means "renovation".

After the war, the reunited country tried to run the south like the north, with state farms, collectives and fixed prices. It went badly. Harvests fell, inflation ran to hundreds of percent a year, and Vietnam had to import food. Aid from the Soviet Union was shrinking.

At the Sixth Party Congress, under the new leader Nguyễn Văn Linh, the party changed course while keeping its hold on power:

  • families got long leases on farmland and could sell their surplus,
  • private businesses were allowed,
  • prices were freed,
  • a 1987 law opened the door to foreign investment.

Within a few years Vietnam went from importing rice to being one of the largest rice exporters in the world. Ties with the United States were restored in 1995, and Vietnam joined the World Trade Organization in 2007. Like China's reform and opening, it combined one-party rule with a market economy, and poverty fell steeply.
sum: The economic reforms launched by Vietnam's Communist Party in December 1986 that moved the country from central planning toward a market economy. The name means "renovation".
